newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hard to see Japan, U.S. accord on insurance - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Hard to see Japan, U.S. accord on insurance - MOF.

text.p: A senior Finance Ministry official said on Friday that it was extremely difficult to tell if Japan and the United States can reach an agreement on their bilateral insurance dispute before a self-imposed December 15 deadline.
High-ranking Japanese and U.S. officials have been in negotiations to resolve their insurance dispute this week before a ministerial meeting on Saturday.
"It is extremely difficult to tell if we can reach an agreement on the insurance dispute. Negotiations are facing difficulties," the official said after Friday's negotiations.
Acting U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) Charlene Barshefsky and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka are scheduled to meet on Saturday in a last-ditch effort to resolve the issue.
The disagreement centers on U.S. charges that Japan is planning to renege on a 1994 trade agreement on deregulation of its lucrative insurance market.
"Bold political decisions are needed to have a breakthrough," the official said.
Japanese negotiators have said Saturday's ministerial meeting is the last opportunity for Mitsuzuka and Barshefsky to meet before the Sunday deadline.
However, the official said there was a possibility of yet another ministerial meeting if no agreement were reached on Saturday.

Washington has argued that the agreement calls for Tokyo to deregulate the huge primary life and casualty insurance sector, which is dominated by Japanese companies, before unleashing competition in the tiny specialty insurance market.
